title: Coming soon: Our 2026 list of Climate Tech Companies to Watch
gist: MIT Technology Review previews its 2026 Climate Tech Companies to Watch list (publishing October 6), framing it against a darkening backdrop: the UN says 1.5 °C will likely be breached within years, US leadership is unraveling climate policy, and Big Tech is backpedaling on climate goals amid the AI data-center buildout. The editors argue clean-tech progress will nonetheless accelerate as costs fall, highlighting energy storage, nuclear, and transportation.

insights.claim: The UN announced earlier in September 2026 that the planet will tip past 1.5 °C of warming likely within the next few years, ending hopes of meeting the Paris agreement's loftiest goal.
insights.speaker: James Temple
insights.so_what: Missing 1.5 °C shifts emphasis from pure mitigation toward adaptation and resilience spending.

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review's annual Climate Tech Companies to Watch list, now in its third year, winnows a long global list to 10 companies judged to have done the most, or have the best chance, to make a real dent in emissions or improve public safety and health; the 2026 list publishes October 6.
insights.speaker: James Temple
insights.so_what: The list is a potential deal-flow and sentiment signal for climate-tech investors.

insights.claim: A related MIT Technology Review piece reports grid-scale batteries broke another record in the US, while smaller residential systems have lagged.

insights.so_what: Utility-scale storage is outperforming residential storage, guiding where storage capital flows.
